title: Finite clopen shift loci for etale-local rank-one complexes
statement:
Let $A$ be a nonzero finite commutative ring, let $Y$ be a scheme, and work on the small pro-etale sites with constant coefficient ring sheaves $A_T$ [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. Let $K\in D(Y_{\mathrm{proet}},A)$ have only finitely many nonzero cohomology sheaves [def-weil-derived-cohomology-sheaves]. Let $\{u_\alpha:U_\alpha\to Y\}_{\alpha\in I}$ be a jointly surjective family of etale morphisms [def-weil-etale-morphism]. For each $\alpha$ let $n_\alpha\in\mathbf Z$ and let $L_\alpha$ be a locally constant sheaf of $A_{U_\alpha}$-modules which is locally isomorphic to $A_{U_\alpha}$ as a module sheaf [def-weil-proetale-locally-constant-sheaf]. Assume isomorphisms $u_\alpha^*K\cong L_\alpha[n_\alpha]$, where pullback is the exact constant-coefficient inverse image applied termwise to complexes [prop-weil-pbc-proetale-constant-exact, def-weil-abstract-derived-category].

For $n\in\mathbf Z$ put $Y_n=\bigcup_{n_\alpha=n}\operatorname{im}(u_\alpha)\subseteq|Y|$. If $\operatorname{im}(u_\alpha)\cap\operatorname{im}(u_\beta)\ne\varnothing$, then $n_\alpha=n_\beta$. The sets $Y_n$ are pairwise disjoint, open and closed, and their union is $|Y|$; only finitely many are nonempty. Whenever $Y_n\ne\varnothing$, the sheaf $\mathcal H^{-n}(K)$ is nonzero. Every nonempty $U_\alpha$ maps entirely into $Y_{n_\alpha}$; the other covering members may be discarded.

proof.text:
Fix an index $\alpha$ and a geometric point $\bar u:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to U_\alpha$, with image $\bar y=u_\alpha\circ\bar u$ in $Y$. Exactness of the constant-coefficient inverse image gives canonical identifications
$$
\mathcal H^q(u_\alpha^*K)\cong u_\alpha^*\mathcal H^q(K)
$$
for every $q$, and [lem-pur-proetale-inverse-image-stalk] identifies the stalk of the right side at $\bar u$ with the stalk of $\mathcal H^q(K)$ at $\bar y$. The isomorphism $u_\alpha^*K\cong L_\alpha[n_\alpha]$ induces isomorphisms of cohomology sheaves, and $\mathcal H^q(L_\alpha[n_\alpha])$ is $L_\alpha$ for $q=-n_\alpha$ and $0$ otherwise. Hence the stalk of $\mathcal H^q(K)$ at $\bar y$ is zero for $q\ne-n_\alpha$ and is isomorphic to the stalk $(L_\alpha)_{\bar u}$ for $q=-n_\alpha$.

It remains to see $(L_\alpha)_{\bar u}\cong A$. By [def-weil-proetale-locally-constant-sheaf] there is a covering family $\{v_j:V_j\to U_\alpha\}_{j\in J}$ of the pro-etale site with isomorphisms $L_\alpha|_{V_j}\cong\underline A_{V_j}$; its arrows are weakly etale and it is an fpqc covering by [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. Lift $\bar u$ to some $V_j$: form $Z_j=\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\times_{U_\alpha}V_j$ with projections $q_j:Z_j\to\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$ and $r_j:Z_j\to V_j$ [def-pc-fibre-product]. By [lem-galois-fpqc-covering-base-change] the $q_j$ form an fpqc covering of $\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$, so some $Z_j$ is nonempty by the joint-surjectivity clause of [def-weil-pbc-fpqc-covering]; this $q_j$ is weakly etale by [lem-weil-pbc-weakly-etale-composition-base-change]. Since $\Omega$ is algebraically closed, [lem-fix-weakly-etale-algclosed-section] gives a section $s$ of $q_j$, and $\bar v=r_j\circ s$ satisfies $v_j\circ\bar v=\bar u\circ q_j\circ s=\bar u$. By [lem-weil-proetale-weakly-etale-localization] the localized site $U_{\alpha,\mathrm{proet}}/V_j$ is $V_{j,\mathrm{proet}}$, with $A_{U_\alpha}|_{V_j}=A_{V_j}$, and $L_\alpha|_{V_j}(W\to V_j)=L_\alpha(W\to U_\alpha)$. In the colimit of [def-weil-proetale-geometric-stalk], pointed neighbourhoods of $\bar u$ that factor through $(V_j,\bar v)$ are cofinal: any $(W,\bar w)$ is refined by $(W\times_{U_\alpha}V_j,(\bar w,\bar v))$, whose projection to $W$ is weakly etale by [lem-weil-pbc-weakly-etale-composition-base-change], and two maps of one neighbourhood are equalized by the filteredness that this definition asserts. These neighbourhoods are exactly the pointed neighbourhoods of $\bar v$ in $V_{j,\mathrm{proet}}$, with the same section sets. Hence $(L_\alpha)_{\bar u}\cong(L_\alpha|_{V_j})_{\bar v}\cong(\underline A_{V_j})_{\bar v}\cong A$, the last isomorphism by [lem-weil-proetale-constant-sheaf-stalk]. As $A\ne0$, the stalk of $\mathcal H^q(K)$ at $\bar y$ is nonzero exactly for $q=-n_\alpha$.

If $\operatorname{im}(u_\alpha)\cap\operatorname{im}(u_\beta)$ is nonempty, choose a point $y$ in it and a geometric point $\bar y$ over $y$. The more precise clause of [lem-weil-pbc-etale-cover-geometric-point-lift] lifts this same $\bar y$ to both $U_\alpha$ and $U_\beta$. By the preceding paragraph, the same stalk of $K$ is nonzero exactly in degree $-n_\alpha$ and exactly in degree $-n_\beta$, so $n_\alpha=n_\beta$.

proof.text: By the Mathlib leaf [lem-weil-pbc-etale-morphism-open-map], every $u_\alpha$ is an open map, so each $\operatorname{im}(u_\alpha)$ is open. Hence each $Y_n$, being a union of such images, is open. Step 1 shows that two images carrying different shifts are disjoint; consequently the $Y_n$ are pairwise disjoint. Joint surjectivity of the family gives $\bigcup_nY_n=|Y|$. The complement of $Y_n$ is the union of the other $Y_m$, so it is open; therefore every $Y_n$ is also closed.
